attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, in his own voice. Not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: The wording matches the sentence. But this is a polemical summary: two parts are value judgments ('cost too much', 'no path to profitability'), and 'can't measure the cost' is a hyperbolic point about business ROI. It is not a literal factual observation.

contract.note: The literal reading, that no dollar cost can ever be put on an LLM task, makes the claim trivially false because tokens are priced per unit. In context, the next paragraph is about firms' operating expenses and ROI. The ordinary reading is that businesses cannot reliably know per-task cost or return. ARC benchmark averages, which he dismisses in the same sentence, don't address that. The contract's own ambiguity flag notes this.

evidence.note: A real March 2026 preprint reporting ARC-AGI benchmark cost per task. It shows benchmark costs get reported. It does not show that firms can measure the cost or ROI of their own LLM tasks, so it is context under a fair reading.

News report of Anthropic's S-1 Q2 2026 operating income. These are company-reported figures, made public before the evaluation date. They bear on profitability, which has no defined measure, so this is context only.
The same report gives Anthropic's H1 2026 net loss, a company disclosure. It is consistent with his profitability skepticism, but that part is an unmeasured judgment, so this is context only.

reviews.rationale: The sentence is polemic. 'Cost too much' and 'no path to profitability' are judgments with no measure. The contract scores 'can't measure the cost' on a literal reading that is stretched against the speaker. In context he means business cost and ROI are unknowable, not that token costs can't be added up. The ARC benchmark figures don't test that meaning, and nothing in the packet settles it. Taken as a whole, the claim is too evaluative and hyperbolic to score.
